title: Treatment for excessive sweating
what: The doctor chooses treatment for heavy sweating. Most often these are injections of a medicine that switches off the sweat glands in the area for a while.
why: When sweat gets in the way of work and life: underarms, palms, or feet are wet even without heat or exercise.
duration: the procedure usually takes 20 to 40 minutes; the effect appears after a few days and usually lasts 4 to 9 months
tell_doctor: When the sweating started and where exactly
If the sweating started suddenly, with weight loss or a fever

prepare.title: Shaving
prepare.text: For the underarms, shave 1 to 2 days before the procedure.

prepare.title: Deodorant
prepare.text: On the day, do not put deodorant on the area.

steps: Sometimes an iodine and starch test is done to see where you sweat most
The skin is cleaned with antiseptic
Many tiny injections are given with a thin needle
The area is wiped, and you are told about aftercare
feel: The injections are quick and many, like mosquito bites
Palms and feet are more sensitive. The doctor will offer numbing
Small bumps and redness go away quickly
after: On the day, avoid saunas, steam rooms, and workouts
The effect appears after a few days
A repeat procedure is usually done when the sweating comes back
red_flags: Weakness in the hands after injections in the palms
Trouble swallowing or breathing: call emergency services

faq.q: Is it harmful not to sweat in one area?
faq.a: No. You still sweat elsewhere, and your body cools down normally.
Yes: special antiperspirants, procedures with a mild current, and sometimes surgery. Your doctor will choose an option.

reminders.text: Sweating treatment tomorrow. Shave the area and do not put on deodorant.
